Primary batteries · Commercial

Zinc–air · Zn-air

Oxygen from outside air is the cathode reactant while zinc is oxidized.

Animated operating principles

Ion and electron pathways

OH⁻ · electrolyte / membrane Electrons e⁻ · external circuit

Simplified reaction directions and pathways. Actual particle numbers and speeds differ.

Electrode and electrolyte principles

OH⁻ moves from the air electrode to the zinc electrode through an alkaline electrolyte.

Overall discharge: 2Zn + O₂ → 2ZnO

Advantages

High energy density in small cells because oxygen is not stored internally.

Drawbacks & challenges

Airflow and humidity must be managed; most consumer products are single-use.

Materials & supply constraints

Zinc and air-electrode catalysts

Main applications

Hearing aids and small medical devices
